editorial.title: Client onboarding checklist: agree the work, owners and handoff
editorial.meta_description: A beginner-friendly sequence for design-studio onboarding: clarify scope, assign owners, collect inputs and agree the next handoff.
outline: H2: What onboarding should establish before delivery starts
H3: Distinguish scope agreement from collecting project inputs
H2: Stage 1 — agree the deliverable, approver and open questions
H2: Stage 2 — record required inputs, owners and due dates
H2: Stage 3 — confirm the handoff and route unresolved questions
H2: Use the checklist without assuming a software purchase
key_points: Reader job: a first-time studio owner can explain who supplies, reviews and approves each input. This is an educational objective (S1), not product evaluation.
Provide a clearly labelled invented example with a blank owner/due-date/status checklist; an illustrative sequence is not researched industry best practice.
Acceptance: the outline distinguishes client inputs from internal approval, and the closing action is to adapt the checklist to an actual project, not book a demo.
Evidence needed: a studio operator should review the sequence; no time-saved number, compliance claim, quote or mandatory legal step is established.
editorial.differentiation: Proposed editorial angle: responsibility and handoff clarity for first-time owners. This is a design choice from S1, not a proven gap against S2 URL-only fixtures.
editorial.reader_job: Reader job: a first-time studio owner can explain who supplies, reviews and approves each input. This is an educational objective (S1), not product evaluation.
evidence_needed: Human studio-operator review of the proposed workflow

editorial.title: How to compare client onboarding software without a feature checklist trap
editorial.meta_description: Learn the questions behind an onboarding-tool comparison, from ownership and information retrieval to approval handoffs.
outline: H2: Begin with the handoff problem, not the software category
H2: Questions to ask about ownership, retrieval and review
H2: Distinguish a notes/checklist workflow from specialist requirements
H2: Record what remains unknown before comparing named vendors
key_points: Reader job: learn how to formulate comparison criteria; no ranked vendor recommendation is justified.
Use generic options such as a shared document and a checklist as illustrative categories only; do not state competitor capabilities.
Next action: write three questions about an actual handoff and use the checklist guide to clarify responsibilities.
Acceptance: no named winner, prices, ratings or purchase CTA; unknown features remain explicit.
editorial.differentiation: Teach criteria before tool choice. The awareness objective favors category understanding; no market leadership or competitive superiority is established.
